annotationRationale: The main route relates the given side product to area and the included vertex angle. Isosceles geometry identifies the obtuse angle. The alternative replaces the sine-area formula with a Pythagorean ratio equation and tangent subtraction.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The condition is s^2=2bh=4K, giving sin(theta)=1/2. In an obtuse isosceles triangle the vertex angle is obtuse, hence theta=150 degrees, choice D. The statement and choices are consistent; no figure is required.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank questions or methods are supplied. LIVE and AMC Mastery Solution 1 are retained in the area route. Mastery Solution 2's altitude and double-angle calculation reaches the same sine equation, so a separate third route would add little. The existing Pythagorean-ratio route is retained as a genuinely different algebraic approach.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed isosceles and sine-area concepts match the main route. Special-angle values are appropriate support. The alternative correctly carries its own Pythagorean, quadratic, and tangent-subtraction nodes.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: For the obtuse included angle, the altitude to the line containing an equal side is s sin(180 degrees-theta)=s sin(theta). Thus K=s^2 sin(theta)/2. Substitution into s^2=4K gives sin(theta)=1/2; the two triangle-angle possibilities are 30 and 150 degrees, and obtuseness selects 150.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The stated LIVE and AMC Mastery Solution 1 references accurately support the route. The candidate adds an explicit altitude derivation and uses original explanatory prose. The third-party-informed basis is correctly labeled.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first move connects the product condition to area, and the obtuse altitude configuration is explained in words. Both sine solutions and the reason for selecting the obtuse one are explicit.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:triangle-sine-area precisely matches the altitude derivation; cnm_137 identifies the obtuse vertex angle, and cnm_h065 supports supplementary-angle sine reduction.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Pythagoras and the condition give a^2+h^2=4ah, hence u=h/a=2±sqrt(3). The obtuse vertex forces each base angle below 45 degrees, so 0<u<1 selects 2-sqrt(3). The displayed tangent subtraction evaluates tan(15 degrees) to that value, yielding vertex angle 150 degrees.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The source description honestly distinguishes the existing graph route and project-developed quadratic argument from AMC Mastery Solution 2's base-angle setup. source-informed-original is appropriate; the method does not falsely attribute its Pythagorean derivation to that source.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The altitude supplies a clear reason to use Pythagoras. The ratio, both quadratic roots, geometric root selection, and special-angle identification are all explained.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_137, cnm_174, cnm_221, cnm_h072, and cnm_278 respectively match altitude bisection, Pythagoras, completing the square, tangent subtraction, and recovery of the base angle.
